Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself to break the task down into smaller, more manageable pieces. Each time the function calls itself, it works on a slightly simpler version of the original problem, moving closer to a final solution. To prevent the function from looping forever, it must include a "base case," which is a stopping condition that returns a direct answer without making another recursive call. Once this base case is reached, all the previous function calls resolve one by one, combining their results to ultimately solve the original problem.
